label: prop:wedderburn-weight-canonical
title: Canonical q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight $\tilde w_\lambda$ and named scalings (BW, LP for all $\lambda$)
html:
The Bethe-Weizsäcker mass coefficient and the LP shadow-price scale the identical canonical q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight:

  \tilde w_\lambda(q)
  \;:=\;
  \frac{\dim_q(\lambda)^2}{[n]_q!}.

The quantum hook-length dimension \dim_q(\lambda) is defined by the q-deformed Frame-Robinson-Thrall formula. This identity holds for all \lambda. No relation between the Markov coefficient y_\lambda and \tilde w_\lambda is asserted: the former "Wenzl-bridge reduction" y_\lambda = \tilde w_\lambda(q) on the self-conjugate stratum is false there and was dropped (see below).

This establishes the central canonicity of the weight \tilde w_\lambda(q). The LP form multiplies this weight by h/2. The Markov coefficient y_\lambda, given by Wenzl's hook-content closed form, is a distinct family on every stratum.

⚠ The Wenzl-bridge premise is FALSE on its own stratum (measured 2026-09-02). The identity y_\lambda = \tilde w_\lambda for \kappa_\lambda = \sum_x c(x) = 0 fails at every such partition with n \leq 6 except the trivial one-cell \lambda = (1) — in the production convention D and in the excised convention C, so it is not a convention-scoping issue:

\lambda \kappa y^{\mathrm D}(q_0) y^{\mathrm C}(q_0) \tilde w(q_0)
(1) 0 1.00000000 1.00000000 1.00000000
(2,1) 0 0.24729789 0.28092963 0.66067377
(2,2) 0 0.06115624 0.06947330 0.16604895
(3,1,1) 0 0 0.01676661 0.29466896
(3,2,1) 0 0 0.00731845 0.35863564

(2,2) and (3,2,1) are precisely the two partitions this block's cited script is said to have verified.

The last two rows are a scope-(b) structural exclusion, not a numerical near-miss. Convention D is the \mathfrak{sl}_2 point of the Ocneanu family (rem:markov-z-reconciliation), so y_\lambda = 0 identically once \lambda has more than two rows — such a \lambda has a cell of content -2, whose Ocneanu numerator factor vanishes (QOU.Information.ocneanu_numerator_vanishes_at_content_neg, sorry-free). Meanwhile \tilde w_\lambda is a ratio of products of positive quantum integers, hence strictly positive for q > 0. The identity there asserts 0 = \text{positive}, and no choice of parameter reconciles it. The other two rows are scope (a): measured non-equality under six readings of \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[n]_q! (symmetric vs unbalanced quantum integer, q-deformed vs ordinary dimension, squared vs unsquared), none of which matches.

What this does not invalidate, which is most of the block. y_eq_self_conjugate was a Lean class field (until 2026-09-04) — assumed, not proved — so nothing in the corpus was ever proved wrong by its falsity. What followed, while it stood, was that the class had no inhabitant carrying the intended y and \tilde w together, so any [WedderburnWeightCanonical R]-conditional result was vacuous at the intended instance rather than false. WedderburnWeightCanonical.beta_mul_h_eq_neg_C, the file's one real theorem, is untouched — its proof uses beta_eq and C_eq only and never reads the y field, so the BW and LP scalings \beta_\lambda = -\tfrac12 \tilde w_\lambda and C_\lambda = \tilde w_\lambda \cdot h/2 stand as definitional. The block's own off-stratum statement, that y_\lambda and \tilde w_\lambda are genuinely distinct families, is correct — and on this evidence correct on the stratum too.

Disposition (owner ruling, 2026-09-04): dropped. Of the three options — restrict the field to \lambda = (1), drop it, or demote the block to a conjecture — the author chose to drop. The field y_eq_self_conjugate and its projection theorem y_self_conjugate are removed from the Lean; y remains in the class as data only, and the class is inhabitable at the honest values. The two definitional scalings and beta_mul_h_eq_neg_C are unchanged. Weakening the field to make the class inhabitable would have been laundering, which is why the choice waited for the author. Measurement: wenzl_bridge_self_conjugate_premise_is_false.py, whose first check now guards the drop.

Notation. This block's weight is \tilde w_\lambda, the third of the three registered partition-weight families (notation register §7aa: y_\lambda, w_\lambda and \tilde w_\lambda are distinct at q \neq 1). The body previously wrote it as w_\lambda(q), conflating it with the Ocneanu/Markov family; the manifest title and the Lean both say \tilde w_\lambda, and they are correct.
